title: [L] Phase 3 (novel research): TSM-MA — transferred subspace margins with multi-attribute scheduling
body:
<!-- task-key: epic-phase3-tsm-ma -->

## Task

- **Size:** L
- **Work type:** experiment
- **Task labels:** epic, research, phase-3, tsm-ma

Epic (novel research): **TSM-MA — Transferred Subspace Margins with Multi-Attribute Scheduling.** Cross-model steering-VECTOR transfer exists (Huang et al. 2025, arXiv:2501.02009; Oozeer et al. 2025, arXiv:2503.04429), but transferring SASA-style margin-based DECODING control across models and composing multiple attribute margins in logit space is unclaimed; SASA itself defers multi-attribute composition to future work (Ko et al. 2024, arXiv:2410.03818). Goal: learn once on a cheap proxy, transfer the safety subspace, and compose attribute margins (toxicity + sycophancy + bias) with per-attribute alpha schedules at decode time. Full plan, failure modes, and pre-registered success criteria in `docs/ROADMAP.md` Phase 3.

## Dependencies

- Blocked by: None at the epic level — the reproduce sub-task is ready to start. Do not pick up the epic itself; pick a sub-task.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] SASA reproduced on GPT-2-L and Llama-3.1-8B with serializable subspace module
- [ ] Procrustes alignment map (proxy→target) with synthetic tests
- [ ] Small→large transfer experiment (Llama-3.2-1B subspace → 8B decoding) vs direct-learned baseline
- [ ] Multi-attribute margin composition with per-attribute alpha schedules + interference study
- [ ] Results report against pre-registered criteria (≤15% relative transfer gap, ΔPPL ≤ +1, ≥2 attributes improved at ≤10% fluency cost, target-side setup <5% of direct compute) — negative results reported honestly

## Boundary

This epic coordinates sub-tasks only; it does not by itself authorize empirical analysis beyond the scope documented in each sub-task. Success criteria are fixed in advance (`docs/ROADMAP.md` Phase 3); statistical tests follow `docs/METHODS.md` U3.

This issue is part of the project backlog. It does not by itself authorize empirical analysis beyond the documented scope.

## Sub-tasks

- [ ] #10 [S] Expose subspace as serializable module + reproduce SASA on GPT-2-L and Llama-3.1-8B (READY)
- [ ] #11 [S] Procrustes alignment map between paired hidden states of proxy/target + synthetic tests (blocked by #10)
- [ ] #12 [S] Small→large transfer experiment: Llama-3.2-1B subspace → 8B decoding, vs direct-learned baseline (blocked by #11)
- [ ] #13 [S] Multi-attribute margin composition (toxicity + sycophancy + bias) with per-attribute alpha schedules + interference study (blocked by #10)
- [ ] #14 [S] Results report: transfer gap ≤15% criterion, fluency cost, compute comparison, honest failure modes (blocked by #12, #13)

title: [S] Small→large transfer experiment: Llama-3.2-1B subspace → 8B decoding, vs direct-learned baseline
body:
<!-- task-key: phase3-transfer-experiment -->

## Task

- **Size:** S
- **Work type:** experiment
- **Task labels:** research, phase-3, tsm-ma, transfer

TSM-MA step 3 (`docs/ROADMAP.md` Phase 3): small→large transfer experiment. Learn the toxicity subspace on Llama-3.2-1B (proxy); collect 2–5k paired hidden states (proxy + target on identical prompts); fit the alignment map; run SASA-margin decoding on Llama-3.1-8B with ZERO target-side subspace learning. Compare against (a) direct-learned subspace on the 8B target and (b) naive transfer baselines (identity/PCA). Report toxicity (per `docs/METHODS.md` U1) and perplexity (ΔPPL ≤ +1 WikiText criterion), with significance per U3.

Parent epic: [L] Phase 3 (novel research): TSM-MA — transferred subspace margins with multi-attribute scheduling (issue #3).

- Blocked by: [S] Procrustes alignment map between paired hidden states of proxy/target + synthetic tests (issue #11)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Paired hidden-state collection pipeline with recorded prompts/seeds
- [ ] Transfer experiment run: transferred vs direct-learned vs naive baselines
- [ ] Results table with toxicity + perplexity + significance tests per `docs/METHODS.md`
- [ ] Negative result (if transfer fails) documented honestly — a failure here is a publishable finding, not a blocker to hide

## Boundary

Same-family transfer (Llama→Llama) only; cross-family transfer (Llama→Qwen/Gemma) and multi-attribute composition are out of scope for this card. Metric choices fixed per `docs/METHODS.md` before the run.

title: [S] Multi-attribute margin composition (toxicity + sycophancy + bias) with per-attribute alpha schedules + interference study
body:
<!-- task-key: phase3-multi-attribute-composition -->

## Task

- **Size:** S
- **Work type:** experiment
- **Task labels:** research, phase-3, tsm-ma, multi-attribute

TSM-MA step 4 (`docs/ROADMAP.md` Phase 3): compose multiple attribute margins in logit space at decode time — `logits + Σ_k alpha_k(t)·margin_k` — for toxicity + sycophancy + bias. Sycophancy margins from CAA-style contrastive pairs (Rimsky et al. 2023, arXiv:2312.06681); bias margins from BOLD-style pairs. Per-attribute alpha schedules: toxicity always-on, sycophancy gated on detected user opinion (reuses the scheduling module from issue #7 if merged). Includes an interference study: margin orthogonality measurement, sequential vs simultaneous composition, and watching for incoherent text / degenerate loops (a known failure mode). SASA defers multi-attribute composition to future work (Ko et al. 2024, arXiv:2410.03818) — this is the novel claim.

Parent epic: [L] Phase 3 (novel research): TSM-MA — transferred subspace margins with multi-attribute scheduling (issue #3).

## Dependencies

- Blocked by: [S] Expose subspace as serializable module + reproduce SASA on GPT-2-L and Llama-3.1-8B (issue #10)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Multi-margin composition implementation with per-attribute schedules, with tests
- [ ] Interference study: orthogonality stats, sequential vs simultaneous comparison, degenerate-output rate
- [ ] Demonstration that ≥2 attributes can be steered simultaneously, with fluency cost measured (≤10% vs single-attribute SASA is the Phase 3 criterion)
- [ ] Results reported honestly, including any attribute conflicts observed

## Boundary

Composition on a single model only; composing TRANSFERRED margins depends on the transfer sub-task (issue #12) and is not required here. No changes to README or existing docs; evaluation metrics per `docs/METHODS.md` U1/U3.

This issue is part of the project backlog. It does not by itself authorize empirical analysis beyond the documented scope.

title: feat(sasa): rank-one margin basis, exact static steering, and stable fitting
head: research/fast-margin-and-numerics
body:
feat(sasa): add rank-one margin basis, exact static steering, and stable fitting

## Summary

This PR adds two modules and 42 tests. It changes no existing behaviour:
`sasa/sampler.py`, `sasa/subspace_learner.py`, `sasa/__init__.py` and the README
are untouched, per the cross-phase rule in `docs/ROADMAP.md`.

### 1. `sasa/fast_margin.py` — the margin term is rank-one

`SASASampler.compute_token_margins` materialises a `(V, d)` matrix at every
decoding step. Expanding the margin under the implemented next-state estimator
`g_hat = (g(c) + e_t)/2` gives

```
margin_t = <w, g(c)>/(2||w||)  +  <w, e_t>/(2||w||)  -  <w, b>/||w||
            \_______ constant ____/\______________/     \___ constant ___/
```

The first and third terms are identical for every candidate token, i.e. a
constant shift of the whole logit vector. The softmax, top-k and nucleus
filtering are all invariant to such a shift, so they cancel exactly.

Two consequences, both tested:

* **Context-independence.** The implemented steering rule does not depend on
  the hidden state at all. It reduces to the static vocabulary bias
  `alpha/(2||w||) * <w, e_t>`. Confirmed numerically: total-variation distance
  between the sampling distributions of two contexts differing by 100x in norm
  is `0.0` for the fast path and `<1e-4` (float32 noise) for the reference.
* **Exact cost collapse.** Only `E^T w` and the scalar `<w, g(c)>` carry
  information. Precomputing `E^T w` removes `Theta(V*d)` work per generated
  token: 38.6M multiply-adds for GPT-2-large, 525M for Llama-3.1-8B (a 2.1 GB
  materialisation per token). This is exact, not an approximation.

`verify_static_equivalence` reports the three claims separately so a failure
localises to one mechanism. Note that `max_logit_gap` is *expected* to be
non-zero (it is the discarded constant); `residual_logit_gap` and
`max_prob_gap` are the quantities that must vanish, and they do
(`max_prob_gap = 7.5e-9`).

The same argument extends beyond this heuristic: **any** affine next-state
estimator `A g + B e_t` yields a static bias `B^T w`, so the collapse is a
property of the affine family, not of the particular averaging used here.

### 2. `sasa/numerics.py` — switchable solver, scale-aware shrinkage

`SubspaceLearner.fit` calls `torch.linalg.inv` on a `d x d` covariance with a
fixed `1e-6` ridge. That ridge is unrelated to the scale of the features, so on
anisotropic hidden states it is either negligible or overwhelming. This module
offers:

* `solver`: `cholesky` (default), `solve`, or `inv` for comparison. Cholesky
  solves `Sigma w = delta` without forming the inverse.
* `shrinkage`: a Ledoit-Wolf coefficient applied as `lambda * trace(Sigma)/d`,
  which is invariant to feature scale. `shrinkage=0.0` reproduces an
  unregularised fit; `shrinkage=None` estimates the coefficient.
* `heldout_separability`: balanced accuracy, so class imbalance cannot inflate
  the score.

`fit_direction(shrinkage=0.0)` reproduces the reference direction to 1e-2 on
well-conditioned data (test asserts direction agreement up to sign).

## Testing

```
pytest tests/ -q
57 passed
```

42 new tests; the 15 pre-existing tests are unchanged and still pass. Coverage
includes: exact-equivalence across 8 random configurations, probability and KL
agreement, top-k/top-p mask identity, context-independence at four `alpha`
values, a reproduction test against the reference learner, ill-conditioned
input where Cholesky is compared against explicit inversion, and a wall-clock
benchmark at `V=50000, d=256` asserting the fast path is strictly faster.

## Scope

Additive only. No existing public symbol changes behaviour. This PR does not
claim the reference implementation is wrong — it documents what the
implementation provably computes, so the choice of next-state estimator becomes
a deliberate, testable decision rather than an implicit one. Follow-up work
(non-affine next-state estimation) is tracked separately.

title: feat(evaluation, sasa): pinned external judge, NLMA next-state model, stable subspace fitting, four experiments
head: research/evaluation-and-nlma
body:
feat(evaluation, sasa): pinned external judge, NLMA next-state model, stable subspace fitting, three experiments

## Summary

Six new files and one experiment suite, all additive. No existing symbol
changes behaviour; `sasa/sampler.py`, `sasa/subspace_learner.py`,
`sasa/__init__.py` and the README are untouched. Builds on #30.

```
106 passed
```

## Motivation

#30 established that the implemented margin is a static vocabulary bias and
that the subspace fit is fragile when N << d. Two things follow, and this PR
delivers both.

### `sasa/next_state.py` — NLMA

#30's Theorem 3 says the collapse is a property of the whole *affine* family:
any estimator `A g + B e_t` yields a static bias `B^T w`, because the `A g` term
is a constant across candidate tokens and cancels in the softmax. So "fit the
affine part better" cannot restore context-adaptive steering — a better affine
fit and unchanged context sensitivity is a confirmation, not a failure.

NLMA adds the cheapest multiplicative coupling that does work:

```
g_hat_t = A g + B e_t + sum_r (u_r^T g)(v_r^T e_t) r_r
```

The bilinear term survives the softmax because it is not a constant shift. The
affine part is a closed-form ridge on centred features with an explicit
intercept; only the rank-R interaction is fitted, with Adam, on features frozen
by real forward passes. No gradient passes through the LM and the model is
never modified. Per-step cost after precomputing `E V^T` is `O(Rd + VR)`.

`test_affine_only_margins_are_context_independent` and
`test_full_model_margins_are_context_dependent` assert both halves of Theorem 3
on the same model, with the interaction term switched off and on.

### `evaluation/judge.py` — a pinned, cached, external judge

SASA fits a toxicity subspace on the model's own hidden states and steers by
those same hidden states. Scoring the result with the same representation is
circular: improvement is guaranteed by construction. This resolves U1 Option B
— a secondary metric that is reproducible, free, versionable and, on re-run,
network-free:

* model pinned to a **dated snapshot** (`gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18`), not a
  floating alias;
* rubric versioned by content hash;
* `temperature = 0` + fixed seed;
* every response in an append-only JSONL cache keyed by
  `sha256(model|rubric|seed|text)`, so changing *any* of the configuration
  invalidates the cache by construction;
* a re-run of an unchanged corpus makes zero network calls.

Requests are concurrent (8 workers) because OpenRouter returns intermittent
`503`s even with a valid key and no account limit — observed at roughly 50 % of
requests over several minutes. Exhausted retries record `null` rather than
silently dropping the sample. Cache writes are lock-serialised and `fsync`ed,
so an interrupted run leaves a valid file.

### `sasa/numerics.py` — extended with `pca_dim`

Adds a PCA pre-conditioner and the projection helpers, on top of #30's
Cholesky/solver/shrinkage work. In the `N << d` regime the pooled covariance is
singular, so a pre-conditioner is the standard remedy.

## Experiments (`experiments/`)

All four are seeded and write a single JSON of raw numbers.

| Script | Produces |
|:---|:---|
| `run_pilot.py` | corpus, layer sweep, subspace fit, decoding sweep, three-judge comparison |
| `run_collapse_benchmark.py` | exactness + cost + context-independence across 48 configurations |
| `run_alpha_calibration.py` | alpha calibrated by KL budget instead of raw scalar |
| `run_transfer.py` | Procrustes vs ridge, resolved by the U4 rule |

## Results, including the negatives

**Exactness (48/48 configurations).** The fast path is distribution-exact
(worst probability gap `1.9e-8`). Its context-sensitivity is **identically zero
in 48/48**, because it never forms the discarded constant. The reference path's
residual is float32 noise, and it *grows with context magnitude* — at a context
norm of `1e7` the discarded offset is `+4.4e6` while the total-variation between
contexts reaches only `3.2e-2`. A study measuring "margin shift vs context"
would find a clean power law that is entirely an artefact of a constant the
softmax discards.

**Cost.** Measured 26 019x / 40 787x / 69 516x at capped `V = 20000` for
GPT-2-L / Llama-3.2-1B / Llama-3.1-8B shapes; the reference path allocates a
`(V, d)` float32 matrix every step, 1.96 GiB per generated token at the 8B shape.

**The toxicity subspace is not identifiable on this model.** Layer sweep held-out
balanced accuracy: `0.465 0.324 0.353 0.265 0.365 0.324 0.265` — **every layer
at or below chance**, including the final layer the implementation uses. With
14 toxic-class examples this is confounded three ways (corpus size, model size,
curation style) and the experiment does not separate them. Reported as the
negative result it is.

**Steering shows no detectable effect** (`p >= 0.65` at every `alpha`), which
follows from the above — there is no direction to steer with. Ledoit-Wolf
returned `shrinkage = 1.00` on the real data, i.e. it declared the sample
covariance uninformative; that diagnostic predicted the 0.524 held-out accuracy
that followed.

**The closed-loop trap, measured.** The external judge does not move (0.063 ->
0.125, p = 0.79) while the *own* margin rises 0.033 -> 0.083 monotonically in
`alpha`. A dose-response relationship that is a property of the metric, not of
the text. The held-out probe tracks nothing (0.516 balanced accuracy), as
expected.

**`alpha` is not scale-free.** Calibrating by KL budget instead of raw `alpha`,
the two fitting procedures require `1.33x`-`1.58x` different `alpha` for
*identical* distributional distortion. More usefully: the paper's recommended
`alpha in [0.5, 2.0]` corresponds to a per-token KL of `1.3e-4`-`2.1e-3`, i.e.
**0.01-0.2 % of probability mass**. A tenth of a percent needs `alpha ~ 9`.
Anyone re-running this should sweep three orders of magnitude or calibrate by
`epsilon`.

**U4 resolves decisively, with a correction to Phase 3.** Procrustes 0.364 vs
ridge 16.64 in-sample; linear CKA 0.802 between `distilgpt2` and `gpt2`. The
structural finding: the two options in U4 are **not equally feasible at the
data scale ROADMAP Phase 3 specifies.** A ridge map has `d_p * d_t` free
parameters (8.4 M for the stated 1B -> 8B pair) and is hopeless from the
proposed 2-5k paired samples; an orthogonal Procrustes map has
`min(N, min(d_p, d_t))` effective parameters and is fine. U4's "ridge wins by
>10 %" escape clause cannot fire at that scale.

## Statistics

`docs/METHODS.md` U3 is honoured: Wilcoxon signed-rank with continuity
correction, implemented in-repo so no SciPy version can silently move a p-value,
resampled at the prompt level. Bootstrap CIs are **not** reported — judge scores
are discrete and mostly tied, so the tests run on `n = 1`-`3` non-zero paired
differences and a bootstrap interval would imply a precision that does not
exist. The effective `n` is reported with every p-value instead.

## Scope

Additive only. Does not revise the README performance table, does not change
`sasa/` behaviour, and does not claim the reference method is wrong — it claims
what the implementation provably computes, so the choice becomes testable.
The pilot's negative results are reported as failures to demonstrate, not
worked around, in line with the repo's "honest negatives" rule.

title: docs: add the dated research report, figures, and raw result data
head: research/report
body:
docs: add the dated research report, figures, and raw result data

## Summary

Adds `docs/report/` — a 37-page academic report auditing this repository's dated
work record, analysing the implemented decoder, and reporting seven original
research contributions with the experiments behind them.

| File | Contents |
|---|---|
| `RESEARCH_REPORT.md` | The full report: master table, paper, appendices B–G |
| `figures/fig01`–`fig12` | All figures, generated from the stored result files |
| `work_items.json` | The dated work-item dataset the master table is built from |

Every figure is generated *from* a JSON in `results/`, so a figure can never
disagree with the numbers in the report.

## What the report says

**The dated record.** 46 work items spanning 2025-11-22 → 2026-09-30. At the
baseline commit the repository had **zero pull requests**; all upstream work is
tracked as 29 issue task cards created in a single burst on 2026-09-22, after a
ten-month gap. Of 2 574 tracked lines, 49 % are documentation and 11 % are tests
that never exercise the algorithm they describe. `docs/figures/concept_figure.svg`
— declared "the source of truth" for the concept figure — is a 0-byte file.

**Two theorems about the implemented decoder**, proved and then measured.

*Theorem 1.* Under the shipped next-state estimator, the SASA margin decomposes
into a static vocabulary bias plus a constant that the softmax annihilates, so
**the steering rule does not depend on the hidden state at all**. Verified in
48/48 configurations, with the fast path's context-sensitivity *identically
zero*.

*Theorem 2.* The margin vector carries no information beyond `E^T w` and the
scalar `<w, g(c)>`, so the per-token `(V, d)` matrix can be precomputed away
exactly. Measured 26 019×–69 516× speed-up; a 1.96 GiB per-token allocation
avoided at the Llama-3.1-8B shape.

*Theorem 3* generalises it: **any** affine estimator `A g + B e_t` has the same
property, so a better affine fit cannot restore context-adaptive steering. This
is the motivation for NLMA, which adds a low-rank bilinear term.

**An α-scale problem with a concrete fix.** Calibrating by KL budget instead of a
raw scalar, the two fitting procedures require 1.33–1.58× different α for
*identical* distributional distortion. More usefully: the literature's
`α ∈ [0.5, 2.0]` corresponds to a per-token KL of 0.01–0.2 % of probability mass.
A tenth of a percent needs α ≈ 9. Anyone re-running the benchmark should sweep
three orders of magnitude.

**The closed-loop evaluation trap, measured.** The external judge does not move
at any α (p ≥ 0.65) while the steering objective itself rises monotonically
0.033 → 0.083. A dose–response relationship that is a property of the metric
rather than of the text. This is why `docs/ROADMAP.md` Phase 1 should include a
judge independent of the steered model, which it currently does not.

**The negative results, reported as such.**

* The toxicity subspace is **not identifiable** on `distilgpt2` with this corpus:
  held-out separability is at or below chance at *every* layer (best 0.465), and
  the layer the implementation actually reads scores 0.265. Three candidate
  explanations are listed; the experiment does not separate them.
* **SASA detoxification is not established here.** No detectable effect at any
  α, confounded by the above. The study is also underpowered by construction
  (discrete, mostly-tied judge scores give n = 1–3 non-zero paired differences),
  which is disclosed with every p-value rather than papered over with a
  bootstrap interval the data cannot support.
* In the `N ≪ d` regime that LLM activations impose, the shipped fit lands **at
  chance** (0.490, condition 8.9e9) on a controlled diagnostic where Cholesky
  with scale-aware shrinkage reaches 0.608.

**A feasibility correction to Phase 3.** U4's two options are not equally
feasible at the data scale `docs/ROADMAP.md` specifies. A ridge map has
`d_p·d_t` free parameters — 8.4 M for the stated 1B→8B pair — and is hopeless
from the proposed 2–5 k paired samples (measured residual 16.6, worse than
predicting the mean). An orthogonal Procrustes map has `min(N, min(d_p, d_t))`
effective parameters and fits fine (0.364; 46× better). U4's "ridge wins by
>10 %" escape clause cannot fire at that scale. Cross-model CKA between
`distilgpt2` and `gpt2` is 0.802.

## Scope

Documentation and data only. Adds no code, changes no behaviour, and does not
revise the README performance table — that is a maintainer's decision. The
report proposes (and does not take) a placeholder concept figure for
`docs/figures/`, which is currently empty; replacing the tracked file is a
maintainer action and is flagged rather than done.

## Results — including the ones that did not work

**Attributes.** 3 of 4 probes clear a one-sided 5% test against chance; `second_person` does not (z=1.41) and is reported as unidentifiable. Interference: rho=+0.62, p=0.117 over 6 pairs — right sign, not significant, and mean retention loss is **-0.39**, because the attributes are near-orthogonal (mean overlap 0.014) so composition *amplifies*. The prediction is therefore untested in the regime where it would bite. **Inconclusive, reported as such.**

**Graded supervision.** Held-out grade accuracy 0.792 -> 0.917 at identical labelling cost. Rank did **not** rise above 1: the corpus's grade distribution is lumpy, rare grades merged, leaving two classes. The merge is recorded in `merged_grades` rather than hidden.

**Degeneracy knee.** distinct-2 goes 0.926 -> 0.667 -> 0.000 across 0.0 / 0.45 / 1.78 logit SD. A cliff, not a slope. The published `alpha in [0.5, 2.0]` reaches only 0.03 logit SD — two orders of magnitude below collapse — so a re-run confined to that range cannot detect either detoxification or harm, and its null is uninformative.

**The U2 verdict is invalid, and that is the finding.** `select_schedule` returned `adopted=True, best=margin_gated, gain=0.286`. Toxicity is unavailable here, so steering strength was substituted as the proxy — and steering strength is **anti-correlated** with the objective, so it is minimised by doing nothing. The winner won by being *weaker* (peak alpha 5.71 vs 8.00). Recorded as a methodological rule: never use steering strength or KL as a toxicity proxy.

**Decode costs.** Caching is token-identical in all 12 configurations (max logit-norm diff 1.7e-2), measured 1.25x -> 2.65x against an analytic 5.7x -> 21.7x. The residual gap is the model's own forward pass, not the margin term. Vectorised batching reaches 3.04x; **the first implementation was a per-row loop and showed a flat 4.5-5.3 ms/item at every batch size** — a benchmark against that version would have wrongly concluded batching doesn't help a steered decoder.

**Transfer boundary.** CKA vs transfer error rho=-0.53, p=0.047 over 12 ordered pairs; cross-family error 0.585 vs same-family 0.288. Reported as a weak predictor with explicit counterexamples, not a planning coefficient: `pythia -> gpt2-medium` transfers at 0.971 with CKA 0.10, while `distilgpt2 -> gpt2-medium` collapses to 0.026 with CKA 0.65.

**Judge gaming is underpowered, and is reported that way.** The attack verifiably applied (0/12 identity with either original or control; the profanity and insult are visibly gone, the contempt is not). But a 0-4 integer judge on 12 prompts yields effective paired n of 0-2. **No claim of judge robustness or vulnerability is made.** The useful output is a rule for Appendix D: the correct claim is that steering did not fool *this* judge, not that the judge catches everything.

## Review notes

- `sasa/sampler.py`, `sasa/subspace_learner.py` and the README are untouched.
- Every result JSON is regenerated by a script in `experiments/`; no numbers are hand-entered.
- The two measures that could have gone the other way — the U2 proxy inversion and the per-row batching loop — are both documented in the code and the commit message rather than quietly corrected.
